column1: # bios-r2.tsv -- DUMPBIOS round 2, the DISK ROUND: Drvmap, Getbpb, Mediach and
# Rwabs on a BIOS block drive, against EmuTOS 1a7484ab (references/emutos,
# docs/analysis/ORACLE.md; TASK/TOOL07, docs/audits/2026-10-28-bios-storage.md).
# Form: tosdump/cases/bios-r1.tsv header, plus the disk round
# (docs/TOS-REFERENCE-DUMPER.md section 6, "The disk round"):
#   !disk 2   this is a disk table, C: its test drive -- the only drive a
#             write may reach;
#   +line     a prelude: an Rwabs read into a dumper buffer, issued after the
#             case's poison and before its call, not recorded; one that does
#             not return 0 stops the run (no dump);
#   writes    write back exactly what the prelude before them read (same
#             buffer, count, sector, drive), so the test image keeps every
#             byte even where the write goes through;
#   r:<len>   capture through the returned pointer (Getbpb's BPB), PTR_RAM.
# WHERE IT RUNS -- never on a disk with data on it:
#   oracle  HATARI_ORACLE_DISK=<test.img> tools/hatari-oracle.sh disk ...:
#           C: = the test image (IDE master), D: = Hatari's GEMDOS drive with
#           the dumper; A:/B: off.  Drvmap 0x0000000C.
#   NewTOS  tools/mkcard.sh with MKCARD_TESTDISK=<the same test.img>: C: =
#           the test image's partition byte for byte, D: = the program
#           partition.  Drvmap 0x0000000C.
# The test image: tools/mktestdisk.sh NEWDESK.INF= -- one FAT16
#   partition at LBA 63, 130977 sectors (PSIZE below), BPB
#   512,4,2048,32,128,129,289,32672,1; C:\NEWDESK.INF is on both sides (NewTOS
#   reads it, EmuTOS does not) so the two test partitions are the same bytes.
# Not in this round (TASK/TOOL07 receipt): RW_NOTRANSLATE (a physical unit
# number is the machine's -- BIOS-STOR-002, open), and the patched boot
# sectors of BIOS-STOR-004/-005/-006, which need a patch step and a restore
# through the physical path.
# One table per round: a case id is the physical line number and the dump
# header carries the CRC of this file, so it is frozen once measured.
!disk
# ---- BIOS 10 Drvmap -- EXACT per profile: both setups are C: + D: (0xC)

column5: Drvmap() C: test, D: program -- bios/bios.c:1206, blkdev.c:833

column1: # ---- BIOS 7 Getbpb(drive) -- blkdev_getbpb, bios/blkdev.c:569-777
# ---- BIOS 9 Mediach(drive) -- blkdev_mediach, bios/blkdev.c:783-820
# ---- BIOS 4 Rwabs(rw,buf,count,recno,drive,lrecno), logical reads --
#      lrwabs bios/bios.c:1045, blkdev_rwabs bios/blkdev.c:406-540

column5: R02 two sectors, the FAT's start -- blkdev.c:430-481
R04 the same sector via recno -- blkdev.c:430-431
R06 one past the end -> ESECNF -- blkdev.c:461-463
R07 straddles the end -> ESECNF -- blkdev.c:461-463
R10 count 0 past the end -> ESECNF (BIOS-STOR-003) -- blkdev.c:461-463
R19 the same sector via lrecno -- blkdev.c:430-431

column1: # ---- Rwabs(0, NULL, n, 0, A:) -- the FastCopy arm: sets A:'s media change
#      state to n and returns 0 before any I/O (bios/blkdev.c:418-428);
#      the second case sets it back to 0 (MEDIANOCHANGE, bios/disk.h:69)
# ---- Writing logical sector 0: the forcechange handshake (BIOS-STOR-001).
#      EmuTOS: a write of sector 0 arms forcechange (blkdev.c:450-453); the
#      write itself then fails E_CHNG without RW_NOMEDIACH (blkdev.c:473-477,
#      blkdev_mediach :799-803); every logical access fails E_CHNG, with
#      RW_NOMEDIACH too, until Getbpb clears it (blkdev.c:589-590).

column5: W03 read sector 1 after it -- blkdev.c:450-451
W08 read sector 1 after Getbpb -- blkdev.c:430-481
the last sector of C: into buffer 0
W09 write the last sector back: no forcechange -- blkdev.c:452
W11 read sector 1 after it -- blkdev.c:430-481
X12 write sector 0 back, RW_NOMEDIACH -- blkdev.c:450-453, 473-477
